info.title: IPL Data Platform API
info.description:
Ball-by-ball IPL data, modelled at one row per delivery.

Every figure this API returns is **derived from deliveries**, not copied from
the source feed. The vendor-supplied scorecards and league table are stored
separately and used only to assert that the derivation is correct — 23
data-quality checks run after every ingest, including one that requires the
points table to equal the published standings exactly, net run rate included.

**Conventions**

- Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`, always, with a `traceId`.
- List endpoints use **keyset pagination**. Treat `page.nextCursor` as opaque.
- Rates that are undefined (a strike rate off no balls) are `null`, never
  `Infinity` or omitted.
- Aggregates carry a strong `ETag`; send `If-None-Match` to get a 304.

get.description: Reports only that the process is running. Deliberately checks no dependency: a database blip must not cause every replica to be restarted at once.
Checks every dependency required to serve traffic, plus data trustworthiness: migration state, materialised-view freshness, and the latest data-quality run.
Every season present in the database, most recent first.

Derived from ball-by-ball deliveries, not copied from the source. League-stage matches only; a side bowled out is charged its full over quota for net run rate. Asserted equal to the published standings by the `points_table_matches_published_standings` data-quality check.
Rate metrics (strike rate, average, economy) apply a qualification floor so a leaderboard is not topped by someone who faced two balls. Override with `minBalls`.

parameters.name: minBalls
parameters.description: Qualification floor for rate metrics; defaults per metric

get.description: All ten franchises. Pass `season` to restrict to teams that fielded a squad that year.
A single team by id.
Aggregate played/won/lost between two teams within one season.
Every ground used in the season.
Average first-innings score, chase success rate and toss impact — the questions asked at the toss.
Keyset-paginated. Pass `page.nextCursor` back as `cursor` verbatim; the cursor is opaque and must not be constructed by clients.

nextCursor.description: Opaque; pass back verbatim to fetch the next page

get.description: Both innings with batting, bowling, fall of wickets and partnerships. Assembled in a fixed number of queries regardless of how many innings the match had.
Ordered by `deliverySeq`, which is monotonic within an innings. `(over, ballInOver)` is deliberately NOT unique — the source repeats the ball number on a wide or no-ball.

deliverySeq.description: Monotonic within the innings; the ordering key

nextCursor.description: Opaque; pass back verbatim to fetch the next page

get.description: One point per legal delivery per innings: cumulative runs and wickets. Feeds the worm chart on the match page.

get.summary: Runs and wickets per over (manhattan chart)
get.description: Runs and wickets conceded in each over, per innings. Feeds the manhattan chart on the match page.
Every partnership in the match, in wicket order, with the runs and balls each stand contributed.
Paginated player search. `q` matches full or short name, case-insensitively.

nextCursor.description: Opaque; pass back verbatim to fetch the next page

get.description: A player profile, including every team they were squadded to.
Career batting figures for the player, optionally scoped to one season.
Career bowling figures for the player, optionally scoped to one season.
Overs 1–6, 7–15 and 16–20. Answers the question every T20 discussion turns into: is this a death bowler?
The player's last N appearances with batting and bowling figures for each.
Batting, bowling and phase splits for two players side by side, for one shared season if given.

get.summary: All venue profiles for a season
get.description: Scoring and toss profile for every venue used in the season, in one call.

get.summary: Full head-to-head matrix for a season
get.description: Every team-versus-team record for the season, as a flat list — build a matrix from it client-side.

post.description: Refreshes every mart concurrently and bumps the cache version, invalidating all cached aggregates atomically. Guarded by `x-internal-token`.
